56.t: The homemade kid band, the Woodland Band
56.s: Ory, the Matthews boys and others formed a band of homemade banjo, guitar, soapbox bass and cigar-box violin.
56.q: Well, I had my own little outfit. I had the two Matthews boys and myself. We started. Yeah. Then I had another kid named White. Yeah.

56.t: Beer from his uncle's license and how the homemade instruments were made
56.s: His uncle supplied liquor; Ory describes burning f-holes into cigar boxes and breaking strings.
56.q: Oh yeah? Yeah. Even as a kid. Who, who'd you buy it from? Oh, I used to give it to my, my dad, his partner. I see. Oh. To give it to you then? Yeah. To make a profit off it. Well, they're the only one that had a liquor license on there, you see. Yeah.

56.t: Building homemade banjo, guitar and bass as a boy
56.s: At about seven Ory made a banjo from a bucket, strung with thread and fishing line, and a cigar-box guitar.
56.q: What kind of banjo did you make? I made a five-string banjo. Out of what? Out of ten buckets. Mm-mm. About the banjo. Yeah, the banjo was a cut bucket, half of it down in regular buckets, you know, about this size. And cut it down about there. Yeah. Well, that was the first one. That was the first…

137.t: Cigar-box fiddles and rattlesnake rattles inside them
137.s: Frontier fiddles were made from cigar boxes and cedar necks with dried rattlesnake rattles dropped inside for loudness; he sold rattles for 25 cents.
137.q: He'd go downtown and buy him a cigar -- no, he wouldn't buy it. He'd go down and get an old cigar box and that's the way they made the fiddles.

137.t: Catgut strings, cedar necks, horsehair bows and rosin
137.s: Durham describes how western fiddle makers made strings from gut, necks from cedar, bows from horse's tail hair and rosin from trees.
137.q: Well, they take the cat's gut and stretch it and let it dry out and then cut it and make a string and that's where the catgut strings --

175.s: His parents were not musical; neighborhood boys made wash-tub bass drums, cheese-box kettle drums and kazoos.
175.q: Well, no, neither of my parents was more or less musically inclined, I wouldn't think so. But we've got a bunch of fellas in the neighborhood have got the experiment from listening to various groups that used to participate in ones at the time. And we used to have what you call bands of our own,…

861.t: Boyhood homemade-instrument groups and fence music
861.s: Asked about unusual groups, he recalls Slow Drag's homemade bass, violinists Lucian and Willis St. Diego, Freddie Gould, and boys beating wires on a fence.
861.q: Oh yeah. Drag had a homemade bass. A fun one they called Tone Meters. That's right. I've heard you told us a little bit about that. They used to have another fellow called Lucian who played the violin. And another fellow, he was some kind of a St. Avril boy who played piano, he used to play the…

568.t: First instruments: cornet, then a one-string soapbox bass and serenading
568.s: He tried cornet, then made a one-string bass from a soapbox and played with friends serenading neighbours at night, dodging a policeman.
568.q: Well, no, I didn't. I started on the cornet, but I put it down. I started to play bass. That was a one-string bass. I had one bass made out of a soapbox. We had an original guitar and an original mandolin. Rob Smith was the guitar player's name. And the mandolin player, I forget his name, but I…

601.t: Boyhood band with Skeeter and a homemade kazoo
601.s: Martin recalls Skeeter on bass and guitar and a boys' band in which Martin, given long pants and put in charge, played a kazoo made from a fishing pole.
601.ch: Algiers places, ball games and Frankie Duson
601.q: They gave me long pants to come. Yeah, I was in charge. They gave me long, long pants. Skeeter, Jackson, and Sola. Yeah. Yeah. They got a... Zuku, eh? One of them fishing poles. Henry poles. Henry poles. Henry poles. Henry poles. And I took it and bored me, cut me two holes in there and that brown…

8.s: As a child Garland played bass in three-piece serenading groups with mandolin and guitar for fun.
8.q: children? Yeah, madeline, guitar and bass. Just serenading, going on a serenading, you know. Go around the house, having good times, you know, go in one of those houses, sit on there, there's a good boy named Chicken, and Arthur Banks, uh-uh, Arthur, yeah. We used to go there, his wife played…

127.t: Blues guitar, kazoos and homemade street instruments
127.s: Punch describes how kids made cane kazoos and played in guitar, tub and washboard street groups.
127.q: No, he ain't no really. His native home is in Natchez, Mississippi. But he left there and he's a young fellow and come here.

51.t: Ory's instruments and his homemade first banjo
51.s: Ory lists the instruments he plays, says valve trombone was first, and describes building homemade instruments.
51.q: I still have it. You still use it? I only had saxophone, clarinet, trumpet and... and carnet, bass, valve trombone, I had a song like that.

801.s: Simon made his own bass from a box, their father got him a bass a year later, and neighbourhood boys played penny parties.
801.q: Well, he helped him in the later years. When Simon got started on base, we lived on Bourbon Street, Bourbon and Marais. He took one of those, I won't say soap boxes, but it was a, the thin stuff, but it was a milk can box. Yeah. Old Magnolia box. And they had a boy they used to call Albert Murphy.…

194.s: As a boy he made trap drums, cymbals and a tube bass from scraps; both men recall the fun of jamming on pots, glasses and trunks.
194.q: Well, they had to run me down to record because around the point of the 30s, I was doing pretty good and didn't realize it. When I really started out, I started with those little trap drums. I don't know if you know you wasn't born. No, no, no. We used to build our equipment in our hands. Make…
